caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 378 of 1999
lawyer:
Md Moksudur Rahman, Senior Advocate, instructed by Md Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record ------- For the Petitioner. 
Not represented ------- The Respondents.
parties:
Akbar Hossain (Md) ----- Petitioner
Vs.
MD, Agrani Bank and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Fazlul Karim J: Plaintiff has filed this petition for leave to appeal against judgment and order dated 9 June, 1997 of the High Court Division making the Rule absolute in Civil Revision No. 3179 of 1993 setting aside those dated 12-6-93 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge allowing Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 3 of 1993 reviewing his earlier judgment dated 3-3-1993 in Other Class Appeal No.179 of 1991 under Order 47 rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 3. The suit was initially decreed and on appeal the same was sent on remand. Thereafter the suit was again decreed ex parte against which defendant preferred an appeal which was allowed on contest restoring the suit to its file and number vacating the ex parte decree. The suit was again decreed against which an appeal was preferred which was allowed on 3-3-1993 dismissing the suit. Against the said decree in appeal the plaintiff- petitioner preferred a review petition being Miscellaneous Judicial Case No. 3 of 1993 which was allowed by judgment and order dated 12-6-1993. The defendant, however, preferred revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure making the Rule absolute setting aside the judgment in review. Against the said judgment and order dated 9-6-1997 the petitioner moved this Court with this petition. 

 4. Mr Moksudur Rahman, learned Counsel appearing for the petitioner, submitted that the High Court Division erred in law in not holding that whether the error crept through Court's oversight or counsel mistake if it is apparent on the face of the record it could be cured without driving to the appeal and misconception of fact and/or law of the learned Advocate is sufficient reason for review inasmuch as the High Court Division has misconceived the scope and purpose of Order XLVII rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 5. Order XLVII rule 1 of the CPC contemplates a review of a judgment and order on discovery of new and important matter which was not known or could not be produced or on account of mistake or error of the record or any other substantial cause. Review is therefore by no means an appeal in disguise whereby an erroneous decision is reheard or corrected but lies only on patent error. In the instant case the review was sought for on the ground of misapplication of certain decision cited to hold that the suit is not maintainable with principle that the petitioner's service is guided by master servant rule. Omission to place the relevant decision at the hearing of the suit or at the appeal is not mistake or error apparent on the face of the record so as to invoke the provision of Order XLVII rule 1 of the Code of Civil Procedure having disposed of the suit on merit. There cannot be rehearing or further hearing of the suit which is already concluded by the decision if any that be erroneous to invoke the provision of review unless the mistake or error is apparent on the face of the record. Mere wrong application of law is no ground of review and if it be allowed to do then the scope of appeal would be frustrated. A suit allegedly decreed on the basis of cited decision which even if meanwhile reversed is no ground for review. 

 6. The High Court Division, in the facts and circumstances of the case, rightly held that "Having regard to the aforesaid decision and in view of the facts and circumstances of the case I find that the learned Additional District Judge, Mr Soumendra acted illegally in sitting over his own judgment by entertaining the Miscellaneous review application to rehear the appeal already concluded by decision even if that be erroneous."
